rv.q: Tucker Green has no time to waste filling in such trifling details and her ruthlessness with the text is thrillingly clinical.
Yet, for all its glaring faults, this engaging piece still marks her out as a playwright to watch.
In the course of 70 minutes, it offers a powerfully intense situation but denies us many of the traditional satisfactions of drama.
This is a play that simmers all the way to the boil.
Watching it is a powerful experience, but not an enlightening one.

cn.t: Tucker green's provocative 70-minute drama about capital punishment and justice divides critics with its uncompromising style and deliberate ambiguity, earning praise for intensity but criticism for withholding context and traditional narrative satisfactions.
